title: You like things just because you've seen them

lines.text: You probably like this song, this face, or this brand, just because you've seen it before.
Psychologist Robert Zajonc studied this in the 1960s.
He showed people Chinese characters they couldn't read, some more often than others.

visual.glyphs: 人山水火木日月口心手目耳天地
visual.label: unfamiliar characters

lines.text: Then he asked what each symbol meant. Good, or bad?
The symbols people had seen before were rated more positive. Every time.
It's called the mere exposure effect.
It's why ads repeat, and why songs grow on you after a few listens.
Your brain reads familiar as safe, and safe as good.
So the more you see this channel, the more you'll like it. Just saying.

sources.claim: Zajonc's mere-exposure research: previously seen stimuli (Chinese characters, nonsense words, polygons) rated more positively than unfamiliar ones
